title: R' Abba bar Yehuda (or Yudan)
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: Or Yodan. He is mentioned in Bereshit Rabbah 23–5 and in the work abbreviated פדר״ב 43b: “R' Abba bar Yodan in the name of R' Acha”; and in Nedarim, chapter 6, halakhah 1 [supplied ה״ר]: “R' Ba bar Yehuda in the name of the house of R' Acha” — and Hyman says it seems it should read “in the name of R' Acha.” Likewise we find in Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5–14 that he said it in the name of R' Yehuda (bar Simon). And what we find in Eruvin 6:6, “R' Abba bar Yehuda in the name of Rav,” Hyman calls a scribal error and says it should read “R' Abba in the name of Rav Yehuda in the name of Rav,” as cited there at 8:4. And in Shevuot, beginning of chapter 3, “R' Ba bar Rav Yehuda in the name of Rav,” Hyman says it should likewise read “in the name of Rav Yehuda,” and the word “Rav” is superfluous. And in Avodah Zarah 2:9, “R' Abba bar Rav Yehuda,” Hyman says it should read as cited in the precious statement in Vayikra Rabbah 7:2 [supplied 7–20], where he said: everything that the Holy One, blessed be He, disqualified in an animal, He made fit in a person; He disqualified in an animal a blind or broken one — and made fit in a person, as it says, “A broken and contrite heart, O God, You will not despise.”

notes.text: The work is abbreviated פדר״ב and the Nedarim halakhah ה״ר; neither is expanded confidently here.

The heading and all separately abbreviated personal titles remain R'; every explicit full Rav in Hyman's quoted and proposed chains remains Rav. A title in the saved closing Midrash passage is not transferred to the heading or to the separate Bereshit Rabbah, Nedarim, Shir HaShirim Rabbah, Eruvin, Shevuot or Avodah Zarah occurrences. Abba/Ba, Yehuda/Yodan and the inherited heading spelling Yudan stay visible rather than harmonized. Bar in a quoted reading is a patronymic; Hyman's proposed in-the-name-of chains are transmission readings, not an admitted genealogy or identity. The Nedarim proposal retains his tentative it-seems-it-should-read force. His Eruvin scribal-error judgment and each definite should-read instruction in Eruvin, Shevuot and Avodah Zarah remain explicitly attributed, with their strength intact; the superfluous Rav is his judgment rather than a deletion made in the supplied source. The first-person plural we find remains Hyman's voice, and bar Simon is his parenthetical qualification. The work abbreviated פדר״ב remains unidentified, with supplied מג: rendered 43b by colon convention only; the former Pesikta de-Rav Kahana expansion is not adopted. Nedarim chapter 6 halakhah ה״ר stays literal and unresolved. The old bounded no-match in the selected Guggenheimer chapter is historical, not global absence or proof of a damaged printed letter. The closing supplied ויק״ר פ״ז-כ stays 7–20 in the translation; one whole 2356-character saved Midrash Rabbah -- TE Vayikra Rabbah 7:2 scalar was read, with raw SHA256, selector and actual edition metadata checked. It explicitly names Rabbi Abba bar Yudan for the animal-disqualification saying, but Hyman's closing compressed sentence supplies no repeated personal name/title to replace; that named digital attribution is recorded here only. The later TE scalar also contains Rabbi Abba bar Yudan reporting Rabbi Yuda bar Rabbi Simon, but this is a separate occurrence and does not verify Hyman's Shir HaShirim chain or add a title before Hyman's parenthetical Simon. The digital comparison does not establish printed pixels, correction history or Hyman's other chain emendations. The universal everything, blind-or-broken contrast, precious characterization, Holy One blessed be He, and broken-and-contrite-heart negation are preserved as Hyman supplies them. The longer scalar's additional animal defects, named speakers, parable, proof texts and sequel are not imported. All old English and both original mixed notes plus the current unresolved-siglum note remain exact; the proposed retirement/revision of that note is not applied. This is one additive qualification, and the p001 source hold remains.

The consulted scan of Hyman I, p. 47, gives Nedarim chapter 6, halakhah 1 and Vayikra Rabbah chapter 7, halakhah 2, beside the supplied ה״ר and 7–20. The English now follows these printed locators and displays the supplied forms. The print also contains an additional Shabbat 1:4 cross-reference and wording introducing the surviving saying; these are absent from the supplied Wikisource body and have not been silently inserted into its translation. The work abbreviated פדר״ב at 43b remains unidentified here. The whole consulted Guggenheimer Nedarim 6:1 passage reads “Rebbi Ba, Rav Yehudah, in the name of the house of Rav Assi,” beside Hyman’s Ba bar Yehudah and house of Acha; it is not silently harmonized with his proposed correction. Bereshit Rabbah 23:5 does name Abba bar Yudan in Acha’s name. Eruvin 6:6 has Ba bar Yehudah in Rav’s name, with a commentary proposing Rav rather than bar; 8:4 gives Yehudah in Rav’s name. Shevuot 3:1 reads Ba, Rav Yehudah, in Rav’s name, and the consulted Avodah Zarah 2:9 passages give Ba in Rav Yehudah’s name. These are occurrence-specific comparisons, not genealogy or identity admission. Hyman’s tentative and definite correction instructions retain their force as his proposals; the exact 43b witness and Shir HaShirim chain have not been collated. The closing animal and broken-heart contrast remains abbreviated as supplied, without importing the Midrash’s extra material. All earlier notes remain unchanged.
